assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message passing for random constraint-satisfaction problems turned spin-glass statistical mechanics into a quantitative theory of computational hardness: clustering and condensation of solutions, satisfiability thresholds, and survey propagation. This is statistical physics of disordered systems applied to a new domain, which I find conceptually clean and lasting, and it connects to inference, error-correcting codes and the physics of learning.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina are the credited names and the decisive contributors to the application to random satisfiability and survey propagation. The underlying cavity method and replica-symmetry breaking stem largely from Parisi, who is already a laureate and is not on the credited list; the prize would need to be framed around the computational application, which makes the allocation relative to that earlier work delicate.
assessment.maturity: Developed from the mid-1980s and 2002 onward, with rigorous mathematical confirmation of several predicted thresholds and wide use in algorithms and information theory. Interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, though not urgent.
uncertainties: How much of the cavity method's originality is already covered by the earlier Parisi recognition
Whether rigorous results confirm the full clustering and condensation picture or only parts of it
Whether the committee would regard this as physics rather than computer science

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and their experimental realisation in twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré quantum matter, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable carbon-only platform. The originality and the breadth of follow-on work are very large, and the platform is a clean arena for strongly interacting many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. The supplied credits support a fair theory plus experiment configuration. I recall that other groups, notably Dean and coworkers and others on related moiré systems, also contributed, so the allocation is not free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by several groups within a few years and extended to many moiré systems. Pairing mechanism and nature of the correlated states remain debated, so the interpretation is mature in phenomenology but not fully settled; timing is plausible but could be considered somewhat early.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved
Disputed boundary between the founding discovery and later moiré work such as fractional Chern insulators
Possible additional deserving contributors beyond three

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase show that gauge potentials and parameter-space geometry have physical consequences in quantum mechanics. Berry phase underlies quantum Hall and topological band theory, polarization, molecular and semiclassical physics, and the effect is conceptually elegant and general. Few ideas have reached so many subfields.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Berry are the credited names. As I recall, the Aharonov-Bohm paper (1959) had David Bohm as a coauthor, who died in 1992, and Ehrenberg and Siday anticipated the effect in 1949; this complicates a fair attribution of the first discovery. Berry's 1984 phase is clearly attributable to him, with Simon, Pancharatnam and others as part of the history.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed repeatedly since the 1960s and 1980s and thoroughly embedded in textbooks. Very mature, and recognition is arguably overdue, with the usual caution about recognising a conceptual rather than a technological result.
uncertainties: Priority issues involving Ehrenberg-Siday, Bohm and Pancharatnam cannot be resolved from the supplied text
Whether the committee views this as one discovery or two linked ones
Age and the long delay may influence timing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controllable strongly interacting Fermi gases with tunable interactions via Feshbach resonances realised the BEC-BCS crossover, a paradigmatic strongly correlated system with universal behaviour. It connects to superfluidity, neutron-star matter and unitary quantum fluids and is a clean test bed for many-body theory.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Salomon and Thomas ran leading early experiments on degenerate Fermi gases, molecular condensates and strongly interacting gases. I recall that the JILA group (Deborah Jin) and Ketterle's and Zwierlein's groups also made decisive contributions, and Jin has died, so the credited three do not obviously capture the full allocation.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally mature and confirmed independently by many groups over twenty years. The interpretation is stable, but this follows several earlier ultracold-atom prizes, which reduces novelty.
uncertainties: Incompleteness of the credited set given JILA and MIT contributions
Overlap with earlier cold-atom recognition
How decisive the specific experiments were relative to the theory

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall prediction and the Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, with the experimental observation of helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, established topological band theory as a central organising idea in condensed-matter physics with lasting impact on materials, spintronics and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical foundation; Molenkamp's group delivered the key experimental realisation following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig and Zhang, and Hasan's work on three-dimensional topological insulators, are real parts of the story; the proposed three fit within the credited names but leave allocation questions about Hasan and the HgTe proposal.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple independent experiments over fifteen years, with a stable interpretation; the field is well recognised, and the prize would be timely though perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases weakens the case
Contribution of Hasan and the BHZ proposal is not captured in a three-person list
Credit assignment between two- and three-dimensional topological insulators

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phase separation as an organising principle inside living cells, with the physical theory of active droplets, brings statistical physics of soft matter to cell biology. Of considerable interest to me as a complex-systems physicist, though the quantitative core is more modest than in the condensed-matter candidates.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the decisive discovery of P granules as liquid droplets, with Jülicher providing the physical theory of active droplets. The configuration is plausible; the theory side includes other workers whom I cannot assess from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very rapidly growing field with strong confirmation of the phenomenon in many systems, but the functional relevance and the physical interpretation of particular condensates remain contested. Perhaps still somewhat early, and the prize category fit is uncertain.
uncertainties: Debate about whether many reported condensates are true phase separation
Fit of biology-centred work to a physics prize
Prior recognition in other prize categories could shift the balance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 using Katori's magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye's strontium clock work, giving tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a basis for redefining the second. Significant lasting impact, though the discovery is more technological than conceptual.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock idea and Ye's group drove record accuracy and coherence. The two-person allocation is clear and fair, although others, including Hall and Hänsch from the frequency-comb work, were already recognised and other groups contributed.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across several laboratories with converging uncertainties; timely given the discussions on redefining the second.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes
Whether precision-measurement advances count as a discovery of the prized sort

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated lattice models with ultracold atoms, from the Hubbard-model proposal to the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition and quantum gas microscopes, provides controllable many-body systems that probe questions in statistical and condensed-matter physics. Broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided theoretical proposals, Greiner and Bloch the decisive Mott-insulator experiments and microscopy. Esslinger, Cirac and others are also credible candidates; picking three requires choices I cannot settle from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated, though this field has already received recognition, and simulating fully the doped Hubbard model remains incomplete.
uncertainties: Overlap with the BEC and optical-lattice prizes already awarded
The five-name credited set shows a contested allocation
Open questions about the extent of simulation of high-temperature superconductivity
